title: Dispatch OGF 8: A Second Crack Sends Water Into the Lower Quarter
summary: The evacuation foretold in the orchard prevents a greater loss.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The reservoir wall gave way at its western channel yesterday, despite the earlier repair. Water entered the lower quarter shortly after three. It covered the first step of the municipal archive and washed through the market’s north lane before the spillway gates diverted it into open fields.

The streets shown in the glass fruit had been cleared. Wardens reported no deaths. Five residents who returned for possessions were rescued from upper rooms. Mr. Fenner’s cart, loaded with blankets and three strangers, crossed the east bridge at 4:12, as one pear had shown. He said the strangers were the people waiting nearest the bridge when the wardens called for transport.

The failure began in old mortar beyond the last visible glass thread. Inspector Voss says the graft’s roots worsened a weakness in the wall, but the reservoir would have required substantial repairs in any event. Engineers will not declare it safe until the damaged channel has been rebuilt.

Mrs. Rill watched the water from the ridge above her orchard. She said she wished the trees had warned the city sooner. Dr. Saye pointed to the displaced families already sheltered on higher ground. “They warned us in time to listen,” she said.

The council has extended the northern evacuation. Those who bought fruit before the market suspended sales have been asked to report any surviving images to the Institute. Several buyers say their pears have turned cloudy; one still shows a room no one has yet identified.
